data.title: Orešany – Slepý vrch, an Early La Tène Celtic hillfort
data.excerpt: Slepý vrch, a Celtic hillfort of the Early La Tène period at 544 m above sea level, lies on a side ridge of the Lesser Carpathians between Dolné and Horné Orešany. Iron ore was extracted here on two hectares enclosed by two lines of defences, and the mass of weapons and the deposits of human and animal bones point to the violent end of this early Celtic centre.

children.text: The Celtic hillfort of the Early La Tène period known as Slepý vrch, at an elevation of 544 m above sea level, lies on one of the hills of a side ridge running north-north-east out of the main massif of the Lesser Carpathians, between the valley of the upper course of the Parná to the west and the cadastral areas of the villages of Dolné and Horné Orešany to the east. The core of the hill consists of quartzites and clayey shales linked to a line of sandy and mottled limestones. On the eastern slope, in its lower part, there is also a horizon of phyllites and shales of the Early Palaeozoic.

The hillfort dates from the 5th century BC, that is from the beginning of the Late Iron Age. Until now it had been assumed that the Celts settled the territory of present-day Slovakia on a large scale only later. Karol Pieta said of the hillfort that „iron ore was evidently extracted on Slepý vrch. There was a hillfort here on two hectares, with two lines of defences“.

blocks.alt: A plan of the Orešany – Slepý vrch hillfort

children.text: The first information about the site appeared in 2002, when Z. Farkaš carried out an inspection of the find spot. Within the project Rescue and Protection of Archaeological Sites as Part of European Cultural Heritage, documentation was prepared together with a survey of the terrain, and data about the site as well as the available material from it were collected. The interior of the hillfort and the terraced settlements below the ramparts are at present very severely damaged by systematic looting, which according to our observations began with the „discovery“ of the hillfort by searchers in 1999 and culminated in recent years. In addition to surveying the defences and the places of important finds (hoards, concentrations of artefacts), test trenching was carried out at selected spots in order to establish the condition and character of the settlement layers. It was confirmed that the whole interior, as well as the western and southern slopes below the rampart, had been intensively searched, as is shown by hundreds of small holes left by digging. They are at the same time evidence of how rich this hillfort was in metal finds before it was looted. This is, after all, also confirmed by the extensive collection of objects that it has been possible to assemble. The first results were published in preliminary form (Pieta 2007).

blocks.alt: A small axe from the Orešany – Slepý vrch hillfort

children.text: Within the project Rescue of Archaeological Cultural Heritage, supported by the Government of the Slovak Republic, a trial excavation was carried out at the find spot in 2008. Its aim was to establish the extent of the damage, above all to the lower settlement layers, and their stratigraphy, and also to verify the method of fortification of the hillfort. The fieldwork was limited by the small number of workers available and by the difficult accessibility of the site. Before the excavation the site and the areas laid out were surveyed geodetically.

The test trenching in the inner enclosure examined only small areas on the terraces along the defences. It was shown that these areas had been artificially levelled and paved with stones. In trench I on the southern side of the hillfort, fragments of charred timber were also found on the terrace, which are perhaps the remains of a ground-level building. Abundant evidence of smithing was also strikingly concentrated in this part of the hillfort – iron slag, semi-finished products, numerous tools and iron artefacts – but the occupation layer was partly washed away, mixed with stones and relatively thin. We found a thicker layer along the northern inner rampart, where entirely isolated Middle La Tène sherds were also found in the surface levels. Here, too, it was not possible to identify structural remains. Practically all the pottery and metal finds belong to the Early La Tène period. Above the levelled subsoil, accumulations of remarkable finds of this period were found, which are described below as deposits.

During the excavation one hundred inventory numbers of pottery, 32 inventory numbers of samples, 575 items of small finds and 14 bags of osteological material were recorded. Of the pottery it was possible to reconstruct five complete vessels and a number of fragments of vessels, which come exclusively from the deposits of finds in trench III. Among the small objects, small production waste clearly predominates, followed by awls, rivets, belt loops and belt clasps and their parts (23 items). Striking is the number of clay spindle whorls (27 items), which also appear in abundance on the surface of the hillfort, and a quantity of these objects was found in past years as well. Further pieces have been added to the high number of weapons found at the site so far (the heads of two javelins, two arrows, a fragment of a sword scabbard). The numbers of Early La Tène iron brooches found have also increased.

blocks.alt: Finds from the Orešany – Slepý vrch hillfort

children.text: The trial excavation at the Slepý vrch hillfort in Horné Orešany in 2008 brought a number of new results and insights. The outer rampart on the southern side was built mainly of earth and stones and had a stone facing. The excavation on the terrace beside the rampart confirmed that it had been artificially shaped, but over such a small area it was unable to identify structural features of a production character, which we assume to be here on the basis of the extraordinary quantity of metal waste. The rampart showed no traces of fire; on the other hand, the remains of charred timber were found on the inner terrace.

On the northern side, in the western part of the excavated area (trench II), no convincing traces of defences destroyed by fire were found, but a few metres further east parts of the construction of a rampart reinforced with horizontal beams were found (trench III). The small scale of the excavation could not answer the question of whether we had come upon the boundary between two different building techniques of the defences – a simple dumped rampart and another, timber-and-earth construction – or upon a place where the planned building work was not completed. These questions, as well as more detailed insights into the structural type of this Early La Tène fortification, could be supplemented by further, extended excavation of this place.

blocks.alt: A bronze brooch from the Orešany – Slepý vrch hillfort

children.text: Undoubtedly the most interesting contribution are the deposits identified in trench III, consisting of human and animal bones. Metal objects and large fragments of vessels as well as complete examples were also found here. According to the first analyses (Miklíková/Jakab 2011), the animal bones are represented mainly by cattle and sheep/goat, with horse and pig less frequent, and by both cranial and post-cranial parts of the skeleton. The human bones have not yet been analysed; incomplete skulls as well as long bones are represented. According to observations in the field, these are generally deposits of parts of bodies laid down in no anatomical order.

The truly above-average quantity of finds from the hillfort so far, with a high proportion of evidence of craft production as well as of weapons, but also of hoards, directs thinking about the function and the demise of this place towards the thesis of a violent capture of the hillfort. Some facts, such as the extreme quantity of sometimes deformed weapons (javelins, spears, swords), also suggest the possible existence of ritual deposits (trophies). The deposits that have been discovered might also lead to this conclusion. The osteological analysis now in progress will help to make the conclusions in this respect more precise.

blocks.alt: A bronze brooch from the Orešany – Slepý vrch hillfort

children.text: The violent demise of this centre is attested by the quantity of weapons found, such as spears, javelins, arrows and swords. The drama that evidently once took place here is also documented by a deposit of bones and skulls of people of all age groups. Archaeologists also found smithing and smelting workshops, workshops for jewellery and precious metals, craftsmen’s tools and products. „The bronze brooches, which are linked to Celtic mythology and depict mythical beings, are a magnificent testimony to advanced early Celtic art,“ said Pieta.
Marking of the hillfort on site

: As at many other hillforts in Slovakia, at Slepý vrch too you will find no information panel or anything similar to tell visitors that they are standing on an important Celtic hillfort. Nor will any waymarks lead you to the hillfort. A typical Slovak disregard for our own history.
